claims.text: A machine-learning approach trained on atomic-scale structure and bonding characteristics can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Atomic-scale features and bonding information are suitable inputs for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The model is trained on a diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys with measured thermal conductivities.
Atomic-scale structure and bonding characteristics mediate thermal-conductivity variation among high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning model captures complex relationships between atomic arrangements and thermal conductivity.
Capturing relationships between atomic arrangements and thermal conductivity enables more accurate predictions than traditional methods.
The machine-learning approach will identify high-entropy alloys with lower phonon thermal conductivity than those identified or predicted by conventional methods.
The machine-learning approach will improve prediction accuracy by at least 20% relative to empirical models or simpler computational methods.
The approach is applicable specifically to high-entropy alloys.
The approach may not generalize to other material classes or to systems governed by different thermal-transport mechanisms.
Model effectiveness may depend on the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
Model effectiveness may vary with alloy complexity.
Failure to improve prediction accuracy by at least 20% over empirical-model predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
